title: Overnight Oats
subtitle: No-cook oats soaked in milk with yoghurt and fresh fruit
excerpt: Rolled oats and chia seeds soaked overnight in milk and yoghurt. A completely hands-off breakfast that waits in the fridge and is ready in the morning. Top with fresh fruit and honey.

recipe.sourceNotes: Overnight oats are a modern variant of Bircher muesli, the Swiss breakfast developed by Maximilian Bircher-Benner around 1900. The key difference from Bircher muesli is that overnight oats use yoghurt and milk with no apple as the base liquid. The chia seeds absorb the milk and create a thicker, pudding-like texture. The oats soften completely overnight without any cooking. Rolled oats work best; jumbo oats stay firmer. Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

content.text: The ratio of oats to liquid determines the final texture: more liquid gives a looser result, less gives something closer to a thick pudding. Stir in the morning if the mixture has thickened too much and add a splash more milk to loosen. Toppings go on just before serving.
Combine the rolled oats, milk, yoghurt, chia seeds, honey, and vanilla in a jar or container with a lid. Stir well. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 6 hours.
In the morning, stir the mixture. Add a splash of milk if the oats have absorbed too much liquid and you prefer a looser consistency. Top with blueberries and an extra drizzle of honey.
